subject: RFI: Private deployment — secure local execution, maintenance windows, and SLAs
messages:
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cobaltone.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, procurement@cobaltone.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@cobaltone.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Private deployment - secure execution & maintenance SLAs

Sergio, thanks for taking this. We're starting the evaluation for a private deployment of your runtime in our VPCs and need a concise response to a handful of operational/security items to move procurement forward. Attached is our RFI template (rfi_cobaltone_private_deploy_v1.pdf) — please answer the tabbed sections related to:

- Operator access model during initial install and during upgrades
- Patch/upgrade windows and forced-restart policies for on-prem instances
- KMS/HSM integration and key custody options (cloud-managed vs customer-managed)
- Telemetry and audit log retention when air-gapped
- Emergency rollback and out-of-band patching for critical CVEs

We'd like your answers by EOD Friday so we can present to security and procurement next week. If it's easier, we can take a 30-min call to walk through.

Thanks — Alex Garner
Director, Infrastructure Security
CobaltOne Systems

Attachments: rfi_cobaltone_private_deploy_v1.pdf
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cobaltone.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Private deployment - secure execution & maintenance SLAs

Alex — appreciate the clear list. I've attached our draft responses (redwood_private_rfi_responses_v1.pdf) that address each tab in your template. High-level notes here: 

- Operator access: we support role-based operator accounts with time-bound sudo and integration with customer KMS for credentials. Detailed runbook included for operator handoff.
- Patching: configurable maintenance windows; emergency hotfix channel for critical CVEs with signed patches and rollback artifacts.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) via KMIP and cloud KMS connectors; HSM-backed signing for installer images.
- Telemetry: offline mode buffers telemetry; we provide a signed export package for audit ingestion when permitted.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to step through the runbook items most relevant to your security team? Irene (ops) and Vanessa (privacy) are Cc'd to help answer the technical and compliance pieces.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_private_rfi_responses_v1.pdf
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cobaltone.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cobaltone.com, Samira Khan <samira.khan@cobaltone.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Private deployment - secure execution & maintenance SLAs

Thanks Sergio — received the PDF. A few clarifications before the call:

1) Patching windows: can you confirm the minimum lead time you require for non-emergency rolling patch windows (we typically need 72 hours notice for scheduling across our ops teams)?
2) KMS: for the HSM-backed installer signing, are signing keys generated by Redwood or can we import our customer-controlled keys? We need an answer because our legal requires key control for sovereignty.
3) Air-gapped telemetry: when you say 'signed export package', can you outline the exact fields included in the telemetry blob and whether you retain any plaintext tokens or PII while buffering?

I've attached our security matrix for reference (cobaltone_security_matrix.xlsx). Let's keep the call to 30 minutes; proposed times tomorrow 10:00-11:00 or 15:00-16:00 PT.

Regards,
Alex Garner

Attachments: cobaltone_security_matrix.xlsx
From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cobaltone.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Feb 2028 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Private deployment - secure execution & maintenance SLAs

Alex — good questions. Below are direct answers we will also fold into the PDF runbook before the call: 

- Minimum lead time for rolling, non-emergency patches: 72 hours. We can fast-track with 24–48 hour notice as an addendum under dedicated capacity contracts, but standard installs expect 72 hours to coordinate operators and snapshots.

- Signing keys for installer images: customers can import and manage signing keys. We support two modes:
  * Customer KMS/HSM import: you provide a public key or an HSM key handle; Redwood will sign installer manifests using the provided key handle via KMIP or cloud-kms connectors.
  * Redwood-issued signing: for optional managed deployments, Redwood can provide HSM-backed keys; usage is logged and auditable.

- Air-gapped telemetry blob: the export includes timestamped audit events (component, operation, operator-id pseudonymized), compact metrics (CPU, memory, token counts), and signed runtime checksums. We do not include raw customer prompts or full response payloads in the telemetry package. Sensitive identifiers (user IDs) are hashed using a customer-provided salt prior to buffer. No plaintext API tokens are retained in the buffer.

Attached is a short operator runbook stub that shows the patch procedure and rollback commands (operator_runbook_stub.md). We'll expand it with your team on the call.

Irene Choi
Director, Private Deploy Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator_runbook_stub.md
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cobaltone.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Feb 2028 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Private deployment - secure execution & maintenance SLAs

Alex — quick follow-up from security engineering after reviewing the runbook stub and your matrix. Two items to confirm ahead of procurement: 

1) Audit log retention: default behavior is 90 days onsite, with configurable retention up to 7 years when logs are exported to customer storage. Can Redwood support S3-compatible endpoints with server-side encryption and object lock for immutability? Yes — we support S3-compatible endpoints and can configure object lock and SSE-C/SSE-KMS per customer preference.

2) Telemetry behaviour during prolonged airgap: when the appliance cannot reach the control plane for >14 days, telemetry switches to sealed mode — logs are locally signed and stored; an operator-initiated signed package is produced for forensic ingestion. See attached audit-telemetry-matrix.csv for expected fields and retention controls.

If you need a signed attestation for these behaviors, we can produce a short attestation letter (SOC2 scoped) after contract signature.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit-telemetry-matrix.csv
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cobaltone.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cobaltone.com, Samira Khan <samira.khan@cobaltone.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 14:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Private deployment - secure execution & maintenance SLAs

Team — this is helpful, thank you. A few next steps from our side: 

- Security will want a formal attestation for the audit-log immutability and the sealed-mode telemetry behavior. Please confirm ETA for that attestation; procurement will need it for the SOW.
- Legal also asked specifically that key-control language be captured in the MSA (ability to import keys and audit key usage). Can you provide proposed MSA language or a redline we can use?
- Procurement: timeline request — if we sign an LOI next week, can we target an onboarding kickoff in 6 weeks? We expect the procurement cycle to move fast but want realistic ops lead times.

If you can reply with the attestation ETA and proposed MSA snippet by EOD Monday we'll move to a draft SOW. Otherwise let's lock a 30-minute call next Monday to run rabbit holes.

Appreciate the team's responsiveness.

— Alex Garner
Director, Infrastructure Security, CobaltOne Systems
